 Gold and silver rates today, November 20: Gold down ₹13,310 per 10 gram this month, silver ₹25,000 a kg; what 22K jewellery costs now
 By Upstox News Desk 4 min read | Updated on November 20, 2026, 18:05 IST
 Preferred news source Select Upstox as your Preferred news source SUMMARY
 Gold fell ₹512 a gram on Friday to ₹12,557, its sharpest single-day fall this month, taking the loss since November 1 to ₹1,331 a gram or ₹13,310 on 10 grams; silver slipped to ₹1,75,000 a kilogram, down ₹25,000 in the same period.
 Both gold and silver have declined significantly in November. | Representational image/AI generated
 Gold rates fell again on Friday, November 20, 2026, with 24 karat at ₹12,557 per gram, down ₹512 from Thursday's price. This is the sharpest single-day fall of the month and the fifth consecutive day of decline. Silver fell ₹5 a gram to ₹175, or ₹1,75,000 a kilogram on Friday, according to Goodreturns data at the time of writing. 
 Open FREE Demat Account within minutes! Join now 
 In the 19 days since November 1, when 24 karat was ₹13,888 a gram, gold has lost ₹1,331 a gram, or ₹13,310 on the 10 gram unit most buyers use, and ₹13,31,000 on a kilogram. On the other hand, Silver, at ₹2,00,000 a kilogram on November 1, has lost ₹25,000. Silver’s decline since November 1 has been a steeper 12.50% against gold's 9.58%.

 Gold, 24K, 1 g ₹13,888 ₹12,557 −₹1,331 
 Gold, 24K, 10 g ₹1,38,880 ₹1,25,570 −₹13,310 
 Gold, 22K, 10 g ₹1,27,300 ₹1,15,100 −₹12,200 
 Silver, 1 kg ₹2,00,000 ₹1,75,000 −₹25,000 
 Gold and silver rates on November 1 and November 20, 2026, before making charges and GST 
 How the rates fell in five days
 The fall in metal prices has been accelerating rather than steady since the start of the month. Gold slipped ₹82 a gram on Monday, ₹76 on Tuesday, ₹278 on Wednesday, ₹257 on Thursday and ₹512 on Friday, in total ₹1,205 a gram, or 8.76%, across five days. Measured from the ₹14,602 rate per gram of November 5, the peak of the festival run, 24 karat is down ₹2,045 a gram, or 14.00%, and 10 grams is ₹20,450 cheaper than it was a fortnight ago.

 Nov 19 ₹13,069 ₹11,980 −257 −235 
 Nov 18 ₹13,326 ₹12,215 −278 −255 
 Nov 17 ₹13,604 ₹12,470 −76 −70 
 Nov 16 ₹13,680 ₹12,540 −82 −75 
 Gold rates for the past five days; change is over the previous day 
 The 18 karat gold price today is ₹9,418 a gram. It has come below ₹10,000 for the first time in the ten days. Ten grams of 22 karat, the grade most jewellery is made in, is ₹1,15,100.
 City-wise rates on Friday were almost identical. In Delhi, gold price was ₹12,572 a gram, about ₹15 above the national rate, and Ahmedabad and Vadodara at ₹12,562; Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Kerala were all at ₹12,557.
 Silver has fallen faster than gold in percentage terms. At ₹175 a gram, it is 12.50% below November 1 and 16.67% below the ₹210 a gram it touched on November 5, marking a loss of ₹35,000 a kilogram from that high. Silver usually moves more sharply than gold in both directions, and carries industrial demand alongside investment demand, which is why its swings are larger.
 How much you have to pay for 22k jewellery?
 Even after the fall, however, the jewellery bill at the counter remains well above the metal value. Calculation shows that buying a jewellery of 10 grams of 22 karat gold at ₹1,15,100 would require an additional approx. ₹13,812 in making charges at 12% and ₹3,867 in GST, taking the total to ₹1,32,779, which is ₹17,679, or about 15%, above the metal price.
 Making charges can run from roughly 5% on plain bangles to 18% on machine-cut designs and they not fallen with the rate.
 Please note that gold and silver jewellery rates published online are indicative and may vary slightly between jewellers. Therefore, you should compare rates before buying. It is also important to check authenticity.
